body.text: Indonesia was jolted last week by accusations that the phones of President Prabowo Subianto and a string of other high-profile figures were illegally wiretapped by a conspiracy within the National Police.
The allegations have dredged up a longstanding political rivalry at the heart of recent Indonesian politics between Prabowo and former President Joko Widodo.

For the people of Indonesia, reckoning with a cost-of-living crisis brought on by global factors and exacerbated by Prabowo’s economic agenda, a fresh scandal is an unwelcome distraction. But for Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka, the pain is probably more immediate. The erstwhile eldest son of Widodo was controversially put on the ticket with Prabowo to exploit his father’s enduring popularity and formalise the partnership between the clans akin to a 19th-century European noble marriage.
Now that arrangement threatens to unravel.

The head of the wiretapping conspiracy, the government alleged Tuesday, was Listyo Sigit Prabowo. Listyo, no relation to the president, served as chief of the police from 2021, beginning under Widodo, before being named Presidential Chief of Staff in a mini reshuffle of the cabinet last month. Listyo is well-known to be a close associate of Widodo and was one of few remaining allies to survive two years of upheaval in the Prabowo cabinet.
Three other high-ranking police officers have also been named suspects: Legal Division chief Ahrie Sonta Nasution and Inspectors General Slamet Uliandi and Eko Hadi Santoso.

“[They] are suspected of illegally tapping the telephone numbers of the president of the Republic of Indonesia, state officials, political figures, media, mass organisation figures, NGOs and businessmen,” Asep Safrudin, head of the police’s Criminal Investigation Agency,told media Tuesday evening.

By Wednesday, the spectre of “treason” had been raised. State Secretary Prasetyo Hadi suggested wiretapping could end up jeopardising the security of state interests, including endangering the safety of the head of state, raising the stakes from scandal to possible flashpoint.
